content:
We have mass spectrum data: peaks at m/z values with intensities. Need to identify elements that can be definitively identified based on isotope distribution patterns visible.

We have peaks: 179.0946 (base), then 180.0978 (intensity ~11.4% of base), 181.1001 (1.0%), 182.1027 (0.065%), 183.1052 (0.0032%), 184.1076 (0.000125%), 185.1102 (tiny). This looks like isotopic pattern of chlorine? Chlorine has two isotopes: 35Cl (75.78%) and 37Cl (24.22%) giving M+2 about 1/3 intensity. Not matching. Bromine: 79Br (50.69%) and 81Br (49.31%) gives M+2 ~ same intensity. Not matching.

Sulfur: 32S (95.02%), 33S (0.75%), 34S (4.21%), 36S (0.02%). Pattern: M+2 about 4% of base, M+1 about 0.75% of base. Here we have M+1 (180) intensity 11.4% of base, M+2 (181) 1%, M+3 (182) 0.065% etc. That seems like presence of carbon (13C) pattern: 13C ~1.1% per carbon. If molecule has many carbons, M+1 intensity ~ n*1.1%. Here 11.4% suggests about 10 carbons. M+2 could be contributions from 2 13C, 34S, 18O, etc. The pattern shows decreasing intensities roughly following binomial distribution for many carbons. So carbon isotopic pattern is evident.

Also presence of sulfur would give distinct M+2 at ~4% relative to base, but we see 1% at M+2, less than typical for one S. Could be due to 2 13C contributions.

Thus definitively identified elements: Carbon (C) because 13C pattern visible. Possibly also chlorine? No. Hydrogen isotopes negligible. Oxygen 18O ~0.2% per O, not large.

Thus only carbon can be definitively identified from pattern. However also maybe presence of sulfur if M+2 at 4% but not observed. So answer list ['C'].

Check isotopic distribution tool for reference.
